subject: Post-call: FrameFive usage review + expansion roadmap
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Ari Goldstein <ari@framefive.com>, procurement@framefive.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: FrameFive usage review + expansion roadmap

Hi Ari —

Thanks again for carving out time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we all have the same plan. Please reply to confirm or correct anything I missed.

Key pain points you shared:
- Rising per-token costs on chat experiences when sessions go long (esp. internal content-editing flows).
- Latency spikes during peak editorial hours (US Eastern afternoon) impacting editor adoption.
- Need for tighter control over data retention and audit logging for compliance with internal policies.

Goals we aligned on:
- Reduce per-interaction cost by 25–40% for the Editor Chat workload within the next quarter.
- Achieve median P95 latency under 400ms for 1k concurrent lightweight chat sessions.
- Run a 6-week Dedicated pilot scoped to Editor Chat + RAG embeddings ingestion (30k docs initial).

Current usage snapshot (Q2 -> Q3 trend, attached framefive_q2_usage.csv):
- Total generation tokens: ~22M/month (up 32% QoQ)
- Embedding units: ~1.4M/month, heavy RAG traffic at index-time and query-time

Suggested expansion path (what we recommend):
1) Pilot: Dedicated small pool (2x A100-equivalent) + prefix KV caching enabled for Editor Chat. Estimated pilot cost: see attached draft quote and proposal.
2) Optimization: Enable quantized model variant + batching rules for background summarization jobs.
3) Scale: If pilot hits cost/latency SLOs, move to Reserved Dedicated (3–6 month commit) and evaluate Private VPC later this fiscal year for audit controls.

Agreed next steps & owners:
- FrameFive: confirm procurement contact + preferred billing cadence (Ari / Jill) — action: reply by 2026-09-10
- Redwood (Laure n/Marissa): send pilot proposal, pricing worksheet, SOC2 artifact links — action: deliver by 2026-09-09 (attached: FF_Q4_Pilot_Proposal.pdf, redwood_draft_quote.xlsx)
- Redwood (Dev): propose pilot config and example caching rules + quick demo notebook — action: share by 2026-09-11

Open questions from our side:
- Will FrameFive require data residency in a specific cloud region for the pilot?
- Any specific retention windows for KV/embedding cache beyond standard 30 days?

Thanks — will follow up with the formal pilot proposal in the next 24 hours.

Warmly,

Lauren Bishop
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com

Thanks Lauren — this aligns with what we discussed. A few quick notes: 

- Confirming procurement: looping in Jill (cc'd) — she handles POs and vendor onboarding.
- Data residency: for the pilot we prefer US-only (us-east by default) — we can revisit for production.
- Retention: editors keep conversation state for up to 90 days today for audit/history; we need a proposal that supports a configurable retention window (30/90/365).

Two asks from our side before we sign off on the pilot: 
1) Can you include SOC 2 Type II evidence and details on audit log export in the proposal?
2) Rough estimate for cost delta if we add embeddings-heavy search (query-time embeddings at scale) — we saw embedding spend jump in Q2.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Ari

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: FrameFive usage review + expansion roadmap — technical notes

Hi Ari — quick technical follow-up and a runnable notebook for the pilot demo: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-drive-framefive-pilot-config

Short answers:
- KV cache: enabling prefix KV caching for Editor Chat reduces token retransmission (~15–30% token savings) for long multi-turn sessions — we can tune TTL per tenant (30/90/365).
- Embeddings: index-time embeddings cost is one-time (higher upfront), query-time embeddings cost scales with QPS; for your patterns we recommend hybrid indexing (embed at ingestion + lightweight query-time re-embedding for personalization).
- Latency: with a Dedicated small pool + batching rules we expect to hit P95 ~ 300–380ms under the described load; we'll include simulated load numbers in the notebook.

I'll attach a short demo notebook and an example pilot config in the shared Drive link. If you want, we can do a 30-min technical walkthrough next week (suggested: Tue 2026-09-14 11am ET).

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
